judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals contain a garbled execution date ("the a4. day of February 1995") and define Eastern Cable Networks as "SENET" while the operative text uses "ENET", and the recital that ENET "owns and operates the sole wireless cable system" is a factual assertion whose boundary is loose. Because the ten-year outer limit of the renewal term in I.B runs from "the date hereof", the illegible date is a live mechanical defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital says ENET will provide equipment, support and royalties "upon the issuance to the University of a license authorizing" relocation, while the operative Sections II and V make the Commitment Fee payable immediately and impose duties before any grant — a classic recital-versus-operative tension. The recitals about Hybrid's D2 rights also frame XIII.Q and XIII.M, which pull against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed end date (August 29, 1998) with a commencement on "the date hereof"; the only softness is that the date hereof is illegible in the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits I.B's automatic renewal and XI's termination rights, though the renewal cap of "ten years from the date hereof" depends on the same uncertain execution date. No direct conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renewal is drafted as one "additional term" ending on the earlier of two dates, with the ENET non-renewal escape hung at the very end after two conditions, so it is genuinely unclear whether the ninety-day notice modifies the whole renewal or only clause (ii), and whether renewal recurs. The condition "provided that ... the University shall have filed an application for renewal of the License" gives the University a lever to defeat renewal by inaction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: VIII.B speaks of "the last automatic renewal term", implying multiple renewals, while I.B.1 provides for a single additional term, and VIII.A/VIII.B let the University decline to renew the FCC license and so kill the renewal condition — a real incoherence with I.C's Right of First Refusal window keyed to "the expiration of the automatic renewal term".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "During any or all of the period from the expiration of the automatic renewal term ... through two years thereafter" is opaque: it is unclear whether the ROFR attaches to offers made during that window, to leases whose term falls in it, or to both, and "exclusive right to match the material terms" leaves "material" undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with I.C.2 (notice at commencement of negotiations, but "one year prior to expiration of the contract") and I.C.3 (seven days after a bona fide offer), which do not describe a single coherent timetable, and with VIII.B, which lets the University surrender the licence outright within the same two-year window.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause first requires notice "at the commencement of any negotiations" and then, in a bolted-on final sentence, that "[s]uch notice must be given one year prior to expiration of the contract" — two incompatible triggers for the same notice, and "the contract" is undefined (this Agreement or the proposed lease).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also sits badly with I.C.3's seven-day notice of a bona fide offer and with I.B's uncertain expiration date, so the whole ROFR machinery cannot be timetabled coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Bona fide offer ... acceptable to the University" and matching "on substantially the same material terms and conditions" are elastic standards, and the anti-frustration sentence turns on the "purpose or the effect" of third-party terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its seven-day/thirty-day mechanics have to be reconciled with I.C.2's one-year advance notice requirement, which they do not obviously fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward re-run of the ROFR procedure for changed offers; "any material term" is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on I.C.2 and I.C.3 "foregoing subsections", which are themselves inconsistent on timing, but adds no new conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly definitional, but the "STL Link" is defined by reference to the University's "existing E Group studio-to-transmitter link" for a D Group station, and the applications are to be prepared as ENET "believes necessary", a purely subjective standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definitions feed II.A.2, III.A and III.E; III.B's reference to receive sites "listed on Schedule A" (they are on Schedule B) shows the cross-references in this part are not reliable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Quality and reliability at least equal to RS 250B" and "as ENET believes necessary" are technical and subjective standards, and the University may require revisions it "shall reasonably require".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The refund of the Commitment Fee on failure to agree here sits directly against II.D.1, where the University "shall retain the commitment fee" on denial of the Modification Application — the fee's fate turns on which failure route occurs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but conventional; the softness is in "provident", "absolute good faith" and the "ECC Applications" typographical slip in the redefinition sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with XIII.A, which contains a near-identical fee-sharing paragraph (there ENET "shall notify" rather than "may notify") — a small but real inconsistency between parallel clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Best-efforts amendment obligation with two provisos; "reasonable requirements of ENET" and "adverse effect on the ability of the University to serve its then-existing receive sites" are the loose terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is nearly duplicated by III.E.1 (modification of transmission facilities) with slightly different wording, and both are subordinated by XIII.Q's Hybrid priority — duplication invites argument about which governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It refers to "this Service Agreement" — a name this instrument never bears — and to "the commitment fee" in lower case, and it cites best efforts "pursuant to Paragraph XII.A" from a Section II context.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Retention of the Commitment Fee here is the mirror image of II.A.2's refund of the same fee, and the two outcomes are not reconciled anywhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear sequence: best efforts to find an alternative source, then a ten-day termination election; "cannot be utilized" is the only judgment call.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with II.E.2's rescission mechanism and excuses the same STL/PTP obligations; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Conditions materially adverse to ENET" is a standard but evaluative phrase; the mechanics are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels II.E.2 and II.E.3 without overlap, and the ten-day windows are consistent across those clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite ten-day windows and a clear rescission right; "materially adverse" is the only evaluative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with II.D.2, which reaches the same end-state (STL/PTP obligations excused) by a different route.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It is unclear what happens after the University terminates and then accepts ENET's indemnity offer — whether the termination is undone — and "reasonable discretion" over acceptance compounds this.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: II.E.2 expressly provides a rescission mechanic in the parallel situation while II.E.3 does not, leaving the effect of acceptance to be inferred.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All reasonable costs and expenses, including legal and engineering, in connection with the preparation of this Agreement" is broad but its terms are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.N caps reimbursement of the University's negotiating costs at "reasonable legal and engineering fees not to exceed $15,000.00" and opens "[n]otwithstanding anything to the contrary", so II.F's uncapped promise and XIII.N (and XII.C) point in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause carries mechanical slips ("until the date that is ten years from the date hereon") and undefined standards ("state-of-the-art equipment", "requisite space", "then-current market value"), and the $1.00 purchase right turns on an exception cross-referenced to "Section XI.B.(2)".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That cross-reference is off: XI.B(2) is ENET's termination for University breach, not a "nonrenewal", so the carve-out from the equipment-purchase right cannot be mapped onto XI or I.B without strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It directs reorientation of receive antennas "listed on Schedule A", but Schedule A is the programming list; this is a mechanical mis-citation that changes what ENET must do.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: X.B.5 states that "Schedule B accurately identifies the site and receive antenna located at the current receive sites", squarely contradicting the Schedule A reference here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition ends mid-thought — "begun broadcasting the D Group" — leaving the triggering event incomplete, and "the first date of the calendar month after" completion is awkward.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V.C fixes the first Royalty by a different trigger ("the twentieth day of the first full calendar month after the D Group Station has been constructed and is broadcasting"), which does not use the defined Start Date at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "During the University Capacity" treats a capacity allocation as a time period, and the continuous-feed proviso is drafted parenthetically; otherwise the allocation of cost and control is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with IV's University Capacity/ENET Capacity split and with XIII.N's reimbursement of operating costs, though ENET bearing "all costs" and also reimbursing the University for "operating and maintaining" the station overlaps.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Best-efforts modification duty with the same two provisos as II.C.1; "reasonable requirements of ENET" is the elastic term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substantially duplicates II.C.1 with slightly different language ("digital compression" here, "compression" there), so a court would have to decide which governs post-grant modifications.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is a long compound condition (FCC rules adopted, manufacturers with equipment "available for immediate purchase", "reliable and cost-effective", "no material degradation in quality") whose satisfaction is highly contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires an application for digital compression "on channel D1", although IV allocates D3 and D4 as ENET Capacity and speaks of compression affecting recapture on D3 and D4 — the channel references do not line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short negative covenant qualified by consent "not unreasonably withheld"; the terms are ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restrains the University from relocating the station while VIII.B lets the University return or not renew the licence altogether on a year's notice — a tension in how firmly ENET's siting interest is protected.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined term is introduced as "(SENET Capacity)" rather than ENET Capacity, and the residual definition "[a]ll capacity that is not ENET Capacity shall be deemed 'University Capacity'" sweeps in D1 and D2 notwithstanding Hybrid's rights; the recapture right's scope after digital implementation is described only by reference to FCC minimums.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Treating D2 as University Capacity conflicts with the Hybrid Agreement priority in XIII.Q and with XIII.M, which contemplates D2 being added to ENET Capacity, and the citation to Report and Order FCC 94-147 as "rel. July 6, 1994" differs from XIII.P.2's "rel. July 9, 1994".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite sum payable on execution; nothing to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its fate is treated inconsistently elsewhere — refunded under II.A.2, retained under II.D.1 — but the defect lies in those clauses rather than here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "greater of" formula is broken: there is a "(ii)" with no "(i)", and it never says the twenty-cent figure is per subscriber per month or fixes the population of "subscriber[s] to ENET's wireless cable service" (system-wide, or only those served by the D Group Station).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V.B.1 supplies a counting rule and XIII.M adds a parallel ten-cent royalty for D2, so the subscriber base concept recurs; nothing squarely contradicts it, but the missing enumerator has to be read against those clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bulk-billing formula is mangled — "determined by dividing the total monthly revenues ... in said bulk billing divided by ENET's then prevailing monthly rate" — and "isolated locations in the same facility" is internally odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports V.B and V.C's certificate showing "the number of subscribers served during each month", though V.C's monthly-served figure and V.B.1's first-day-of-month snapshot are not identical measures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Showing the number of subscribers served during each month of such period" refers to a "period" never identified, and the payment trigger is described in narrative rather than by the defined Start Date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: III.C defines a "Start Date" tied to completion of the D Group Station, STL Link, PTP Link and the Modification Plan, whereas this clause triggers payment on the station merely being "constructed and ... broadcasting" — two different commencement tests.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The retention period (eighteen months) and audit window are stated definitely; "at any time or times" against "thirty (30) business days' advance written notice" is a mild internal friction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with V.B/V.C's royalty computation and certificate; no other provision addresses records.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain non-interference covenant with a clear consequence; "lawfully" is the only qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the royalty structure in V.B (which is subscriber-count based, not revenue-share based) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Proportionately reduced" is mechanical, though it does not say whether the $2,500 floor is prorated as well as the per-subscriber figure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with V.B's "greater of" formula and V.B.1's first-day-of-month count, proration of a monthly minimum is workable but not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says the Royalty "is the gross charge to ENET" and then places responsibility for applicable taxes and fees on the University — a counterintuitive allocation that reads as though a party name may have been transposed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Elsewhere ENET bears essentially every cost (II.F, VIII.A, XII.C, XIII.N), so a tax burden falling on the University is at least in tension with the instrument's cost-allocation pattern.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The coverage standard is doubly vague — "of the kinds customarily insured against by firms of established reputations" in "such amounts as are customarily carried" — and the enumerated items follow "including, without limitation", raising the reach of the general words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: XIII.T's rule that "including" means "including, without limitation" confirms the list is non-exhaustive; no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete requirement: 100% of full replacement value without depreciation deduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with VI.A's preamble and VI.B's policy-form requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific dollar limits per occurrence, per year and for property damage; the sentence merely lacks a closing period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits VI.A and VI.B without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]s appropriate, designate the University as either the insured party or as an additional insured" leaves the choice unassigned and unguided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires delivery of policies "prior to commencing operation of the D Group Station", which is a different milestone from the Start Date in III.C, but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of permitted programming closes with "or an other programming agreed to by the University" (a mechanical error for "any other"), and the clause then swings between consent "not unreasonably withheld" and the University's "absolute right to deny" obscene programming — the reach of the catch-all against the specifics is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Schedule A, which describes itself as merely "representative types of programming" filed "pursuant to Subparagraph 3 (C)" — a subparagraph that does not exist in this Agreement — and sits against IV's grant of ENET Capacity "for any legal purpose, without any restriction on the substance, format or type of information".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All licenses, permits and authorizations required or desired" is open-ended (desired by whom?), and "best efforts" plus "all necessary steps" set differing standards within one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The duty to "take all necessary steps to renew" is expressly carved back by VIII.B, which permits the University to hand back or not renew the licence, and I.B conditions renewal on the University actually filing a renewal application.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It permits surrender or non-renewal of the very licence on which the Agreement depends, on one year's notice, and the phrase "at anytime within two years after the expiration of the last automatic renewal term" presupposes renewals the Agreement does not clearly provide.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against VIII.A's duty to preserve the authorisation, against I.B's renewal condition, and against I.C's Right of First Refusal covering the same post-expiration two-year window; XIII.A also duplicates the assignment machinery with different conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second limb runs "(1) ... (ii)" and ends with "any other claimed harm or unlawfulness arising from the transmission of any programming" after a list of specific torts — a general catch-all of uncertain reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ENET indemnifies for programming content although VII gives the University prior approval rights and an "absolute right to deny" obscene programming, so the allocation of content risk against the University's control is not obviously coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mirror-image indemnity in conventional terms; "gross negligence or willful misconduct" is a well-worn standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to IX.A but narrower (no content limb), which is explicable by the parties' roles; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard claims procedure; "in form and substance satisfactory to the Claiming Party" is a subjective gate but a familiar one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to both IX.A and IX.B symmetrically and does not clash with XI.C's preservation of damages claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat corporate-existence representation and covenant; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the mirror representation in X.B.1 and with X.C's survival clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unqualified compliance covenant ("shall comply with all laws, rules and regulations") with no materiality threshold, which is broad but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The University's mirror covenant in X.B.2 is qualified "in all material respects", an asymmetry that could be argued but is not an internal contradiction.
